SpillCheck looks up an email or username against known, already-public data breaches.

This is a check. It is not a leak portal. We do not host dumps, we do not sell access to leaks, and we will not "get you the file".

If we have a result for an address, it has its own page. Paste an address in a client that can open a lookup URL, or use a link you were already given. A blank box on this page does not invent a result.

For a list of incidents we know about, see Breaches.

A partial list of incidents in our index. Names and dates only. We do not publish the records themselves.

If your address appeared, change the password, and do not reuse it. We will not email you first.

We add a breach when we can show, to our own satisfaction, that the records have already been made public and that the organisation and the date are correctly named.

We do not pay for dumps. We do not take "exclusive" files in a private message. We do not publish a download.

A name on the Breaches page means we have indexed it. It does not mean we discuss how the file left the organisation, or who was at fault.

What do you do?
We check addresses against known breaches. That is the whole service.

Will you find a leak for me?
No. We are not a leak portal.

Why is there no search box that just works on this page?
Lookups that exist have their own pages. We do not run a live hunt from this site.

I never used that forum / gym / school portal.
Then someone used your address there, or the record is old, or you should still change the password.

Do you email me if I appear?
No.

We keep the minimum we need to run a lookup: the index of known breaches, and the pages that already exist for particular addresses.

We do not build a marketing list from checks. We do not sell "your results". If you opened a result page, that is a page, not a subscription.
